about:
# QFXSystemBar

QFXSystemBar is a World of Warcraft addon that provides a lightweight system bar, configurable micro menu buttons, info bar integration, locale packs, and MeetingStone-family bridge support.

## Contents

- `QFXSystemBar/` - core addon files and media assets
- `QFXSystemBar_Config/` - configuration UI module
- `QFXSystemBar_InfoBar/` - info bar integration module
- `QFXSystemBar_Locale/` - load-on-demand localization module (all languages, one per file)
- `QFXSystemBar_MeetingStone/` - MeetingStone and group-finder bridge module

## Utility shortcuts

WoW: Forever (interface 16001) uses the same five addon folders. Its talents,
spellbook and Legacy entries are separate; existing talents visibility and
button order are preserved when adapting saved settings. Retail-only Vault,
Mythic+ score, MDT and Midnight crest entries are hidden on Forever. New Forever
settings show the native micro menu and bag bar by default; existing saved
visibility modes are preserved. Random mounts
use usable collected mounts there, while Retail retains random favorites.
Version 1.16.0 declares support only for Retail 12.1.5 (120105) and
WoW: Forever 1.60.1 (16001), using one package. Older Retail patches are not
included in its supported-version metadata.

The optional Macros button uses left-click to open or close Blizzard's macro
window in and out of combat. Right-click has no action. It also works when
QFXAddonManager enlarges the native macro window; that extension is optional.

In `/qfxbar` > Micro Menu > Button Order & Visibility, enable Great Vault or MRT
and drag them into place. Both are disabled by default. Great Vault left-click
opens/closes Blizzard's rewards panel; MRT left-click opens/closes Method Raid Tools
when installed. Great Vault supports combat clicks; loaded MRT keeps its own
combat behavior, matching the MDT shortcut. MRT uses a white transparent icon.

Great Vault hover shows each activity category's completion count and unlocked
reward slots, using the game's current thresholds. In `/qfxbar` > Info Bar,
enable Vault, MRT or MDT in a bar's content settings and adjust their order.
These optional shortcuts display text only; Vault hover shares the progress
readout, and left-click toggles the corresponding panel.

Clock: left-click opens the calendar, right-click cleans memory, middle-click
reloads the interface outside combat. Owned Mycomancer's Hearthspore is available
as a hearthstone click action and in the random cosmetic hearthstone pool.

## Crests and account gold

In `/qfxbar` > Info Bar, enable the five Midnight upgrade crests (Adventurer
through Myth) in a bar's content settings. Each crest shows the currency icon
with its live amount, a tooltip with the weekly progress, and counts as 0.4 of
the bar's five item slots so a full row of crests shares two ordinary cells.

The gold tooltip lists every recorded character with gold totals, the warband
bank reading and the session profit/loss. Characters are recorded when they
log in or their money changes. Ctrl+Left Click on the gold item clears the
records after a confirming second press.

## Group finder integration

The MeetingStone menu button and info-bar item also support GroupFinder,
PremadeGroupBoard and Lychee LFG, in that priority after MeetingStone. Lychee
uses its native window toggle, including combat clicks, and its floating-entry
API supplies live application status and the hover list. The hosted entry keeps
the configured MeetingStone icon and restores standalone mode when released.

## License

This project is released under the MIT License.
Third-party artwork retains its own license; see the attribution and license
files alongside the media. The adapted MDT logo and its editable SVG source
are supplied under GPL v2 in `QFXSystemBar/Media/MicroMenu/`.

## Releases

Local development and game-directory syncs keep the current addon version.
Increment version numbers only when performing an explicitly requested formal
release. Keep development packages separate from existing release archives.

Pushing a Git tag packages all addon modules, creates a GitHub Release, and
publishes the archive to CurseForge project `1533536`.

Before the first release, add a repository Actions secret named `CF_API_KEY`.
Then update the version in all five modules' TOC files and `addon_version.txt`,
commit the release, and push an annotated tag:

```bash
git tag -a 1.16.0 -m "Release 1.16.0"
git push origin main 1.16.0
```

Release archives use the name `QFXSystemBar_<version>.zip`. To check a local
development package, run `python tests/build_release_zip.py`; the default output
is `.release/QFXSystemBar_<version>_dev.zip`. Existing files are preserved unless
`--overwrite` is explicitly supplied. Use `--output <path>` to select another
destination. This does not change addon versions or publish a release.

Both packaging paths omit PNG/SVG artwork sources and redundant theme TGA files
whose BLP versions are used at runtime. Keep these source files in the repository
for the icon-generation tools.

# QFXSystemBar

## 1.16.4 (2026-11-24)

- Stop writing `MicroMenu`'s own alpha in every native-menu mode. Hiding and mouseover fading now act on `MicroMenuContainer`, the ordinary Edit Mode container; `MicroMenu` itself is never given an addon-written alpha. The Forever `BackgroundArt` / `BorderArt` regions are still faded separately.
- Remove direct writes to native micro-button `Alert` regions; `MainMenuMicroButton_HideAlert` remains the only owner. The Forever art alpha is cached, so a visibility refresh no longer re-sends identical writes.
- Reclaim the native `MicroMenu` after pet battles and vehicles. If Blizzard leaves it docked under `PetBattleFrame` or `OverrideActionBar`, the addon restores its parent to `MicroMenuContainer`, runs the container layout, restores the cached home anchor, and re-applies the QFX visibility state. Combat-locked cases are deferred to `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED`.
- Cover the reclaim path in `NativeVisibility`: pet-battle dock restoration, cached anchor, no `MicroMenu` alpha write, and combat deferral.
- Restore the hover enlarge animation on every micro-menu icon, including during combat. The animation only resizes QFX's own Texture and never touches a secure button's click rect, attributes or shown state; the previous combat/`IsProtected` split made some icons animate and others not, with no action-bar safety benefit.
- Restore hover feedback on the MeetingStone button when LycheeGroup hosts its floating logo. Lychee replaces the QFX icon with its own logo texture; that hosted texture now scales with the same 1.2x factor and restores its original scale when the pointer leaves or the host changes.

## 1.16.3 (2026-11-22)

- **Intentional behavior:** to keep the action-bar taint fix safe, hover scaling is skipped for protected icon regions while in combat. Some micro-menu buttons therefore do not play the enlarge animation during combat. Unprotected icons and all out-of-combat hover still scale normally; this is a deliberate guard, not a bug.
- Stop hiding the protected `MicroMenu` frame when the native micro menu is set to hidden. The native visibility policy now hides the ordinary `MicroMenuContainer` instead (falling back to `MicroMenu` only on clients without that container). Hiding `MicroMenu` itself tainted Blizzard's shared `ActionBarController`; a later `UpdateShownButtons` pass could then report `ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED` for an arbitrary bar button such as `MultiBar5Button1:SetShown()`.
- Never issue a redundant container `Hide()`/`Show()`: the protected calls now run only on a real shown-state edge instead of on every visibility refresh. The native menu is also kept at alpha 0 while hidden, so a `MicroMenu` that Blizzard docks into the vehicle/pet-battle UI stays invisible without touching its protected shown state.
- Keep the fix container-only: secure micro-menu/bag buttons, their scripts and their hook tables remain untouched. The `NativeVisibility` regression was updated to assert that `MicroMenu` itself is never hidden or re-hooked.
- Fade `MicroMenu.BackgroundArt` and `BorderArt` while the native micro menu is hidden. WoW Forever frames its micro menu with those regions, and they live outside the hidden Edit Mode container, so the ornate strip could remain behind the QFX clock. Alpha only: the regions are never hidden or re-hooked.
- Allow hover-icon scaling in combat when the icon region itself is not protected. The guard now asks the region through `IsProtected()` instead of blanket-disabling combat hover; protected regions still skip the resize, and the combat-end reset still restores any icon left enlarged.
- Stop issuing a redundant `Hide()` from the deferred native-menu re-hide path and preserve the original pre-hide shown state when Blizzard re-shows a suppressed container. Both were residual taint/restoration edge cases found in the post-fix audit.
- Harden two more post-fix edges: read a secret alpha without arithmetic before starting a fade, and fade a native micro-button alert with `SetAlpha(0)` instead of `Hide()` from delayed cleanup timers. Neither path can now hand a protected visibility/alpha operation to Blizzard's action-bar update loop.

## 1.16.2 (2026-11-16)

- Fix the combat taint that could flood the UI with `ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED` for `MultiBarBottomLeftButton1:SetShown()` and stop action-bar cooldowns from updating. The native micro menu and bag bar are now hidden only through their ordinary `MicroMenu` and `BagsBar` containers instead of hiding each secure micro-menu and bag button individually. Directly hiding `MainMenuBarBackpackButton`, the bag slots or the micro buttons tainted Blizzard's secure frames; the buttons now keep their native scripts, shown state and hook tables.
- Stop adding a hide hook to every native micro-menu/bag button; the container `OnShow` hook now owns the re-hide policy and still defers protected hides until combat ends. Hover fades and alert cleanup continue to read the native buttons without changing their visibility.
- NativeVisibility regression updated to assert that no secure child button is hidden or re-hooked and that container-only restoration leaves originally hidden buttons hidden.

- Fix the combat taint that could flood the UI with `ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED` for `MultiBarBottomLeftButton1:SetShown()` and stop action-bar cooldowns from updating. ## 1.16.1 (2026-11-08)

- Fix the micro-menu clock colon occasionally rendering as two solid black dots. Pin the black outline backings below the coloured dots with explicit draw sublevels, and let the one-second blink fade only the colon anchor so region visibility has a single owner. Appearance, spacing and blink rate are unchanged.
- Match the manager's native takeover contract. Expose `QFXSystemBarAPI.OpenNativeOptions` with native window and page entries that bypass the managed route, and honour a false return from `OpenAddonSettings` at every launcher so a declined manager open (combat lockdown, unloaded config, blocked addon class) still falls back to the addon's own settings window instead of silently doing nothing.
- Fix a drag-reorder Lua error when only one icon button is enabled: dropping it left of the clock inserted at position 0 and aborted the whole move before the order was saved.
- Run the Forever settings migration before the defaults merge at login, so an upgrading player's old PlayerSpells toggle is inherited by the new SpellBook/Legacy entries instead of being overwritten by defaults.
- Keep hover icon scaling and badge anchoring out of combat lockdown, and restore base icon sizes once combat ends so an icon hovered before combat cannot stay enlarged.
- Keep the micro menu fully shown while drag-unlocked. The DIALOG-strata drag overlay never inherits the menu's fade alpha and blocked mouseover reveal, so a faded-out unlocked menu could not be hovered back into view.
- Resolve option defaults lazily for load-on-demand InfoBar keys, so reading or resetting a row built before InfoBar loaded uses the injected default instead of nil.
- Drop a duplicate MeetingStone broker before it takes an info-bar span: a second strip no longer reserves a blank cell and loses that much item budget. The owning strip keeps its broker across refreshes.
- Gate the warband-bank gold query with `issecretvalue`/`canaccessvalue` before any arithmetic instead of probing the restriction with pcall, and make the rich gold tooltip's left-click hint follow the current currency/bag-slot toggle.
- Align settings UI with runtime behavior: icon spacing slider minimum is 0 (the renderer clamps negatives), the info-bar preview line thickness clamp matches the slider maximum of 6, and the manager's info-item grid enforces the weighted budget through its setValue path instead of a raw count cap.
- Ellipsize overlong settings navigation labels (English group names) to the button box and show the full text on hover.
- Add the 8 missing keys to the deDE/esES/esMX/frFR/itIT/koKR/ptBR/ruRU locale packs; all ten packs now carry the same 564 keys.
- Validate 22 Lua regression suites, including new regressions for the drag crash, the Forever login migration order, load-on-demand defaults and the duplicate MeetingStone broker, each confirmed to fail against the pre-fix code. SavedVariables declarations and player data are unchanged.

## 1.16.0 (2026-11-05)

- Support only Retail 12.1.5 (120105) and WoW: Forever 1.60.1 (16001) in the same package. Remove older Retail interface declarations from all five modules.
- Hide both MDT entries and block its launcher on Forever. New Forever settings show the native micro menu and bag bar by default; preserve saved visibility modes and Retail defaults.
- Add WoW: Forever interface 16001 to all five addons and a shared compatibility layer.
- Forward the existing talents entry to Forever's TalentMicroButton; add separate spellbook and Legacy entries, preserving existing toggles and relative order during migration.
- Use C_SpecializationInfo for specialization text and loot/talent menus. Keep the native professional and group-finder button implementations.
- Respect Forever micro-menu game rules in runtime, standalone settings and manager-hosted settings. Hide Retail-only Vault, Mythic+ score and Midnight crest entries without clearing their saved selections or charging them against the info-bar item limit; omit the warband-bank query.
- Resolve Forever's random mount action from usable collected mounts instead of Retail favorites, with labels in all ten locale packs. Keep existing hearthstone ownership/usability filtering and optional third-party entry points.
- Update the automatic packager to 2.7.0 so Forever is tagged with its own game flavor. Validate the exact supported interfaces and version consistency before publishing.

## 1.15.0 (2026-10-23)

- Add Lychee LFG support to the MeetingStone micro-menu button and info-bar item, including localized names, window toggling and late addon loading. Preserve the existing provider priority.
- Host Lychee's native floating entry and application popup through its version-1 API while keeping the configured MeetingStone icon. Support host transfer, live status, standalone restoration, compatibility opt-out and foreign owners.
- Match Lychee's native window entry with a direct, synchronous ToggleWindow call. Combat opening was confirmed in-game with no new errors after reload; other group-finder providers keep their existing behavior.
- Fix session gold income, spending and net displaying zero, and correct copper-valued spending formatting. Refresh an owned gold tooltip when money changes; preserve existing records.
- Stop hidden info-bar/menu polling, share repeated text queries, reuse sorted system snapshots, merge combat-end refreshes and coalesce floating retries. Refresh Lychee layout/artwork only when it changes, and unsubscribe idle placement/combat-repair listeners.
- Remove two unused provider placeholders and omit 64 artwork-source/redundant-format files from runtime packages while retaining generator inputs. Keep existing release archives safe from development builds.
- Validate 19 Lua regression suites, installed Lychee Core/Host/API contracts, all runtime Lua/TOC references and two package tests. SavedVariables declarations and player data are unchanged.

## 1.14.11 (2026-10-19)

- Fix a Lua error raised from the shared settings factory: a disabled row, checkbox or colour swatch whose reason getter produced no text handed the getter function itself to the tooltip text setter, which reported `bad argument #2 to '?' (Usage: self:SetText(text [, color, alpha, wrap]))`. Disabled reasons now resolve to a string, and a predicate that reports "disabled" without a reason simply shows no tooltip.
- Resolve dropdown and icon-picker item getters the same way, so a getter that returns nil falls back to an empty list instead of the function (`ipairs`/`#` on a function).
- No settings, SavedVariables, TOC directives or runtime feature changes; the five modules share the 1.14.11 version. All 15 Lua regression suites and the release-package checks pass; the affected hover paths still need an in-game confirmation.
